A local VPN that only receives DNS lookups. Lookups for hosts on the block list get \"not found\"; all others go to your network\'s own DNS servers. App traffic itself never passes through it. Lookups are not logged or stored.

Private DNS is set to a provider
Android sends lookups straight to your Private DNS provider, so on-device blocking cannot see them. Set Private DNS to Automatic, or use the provider option below instead.
Set Android\'s Private DNS to an ad-blocking provider. It blocks ads for every app and does not use the VPN, so the firewall can stay on.
Settings → Network & internet → Private DNS → Private DNS provider hostname. The provider (AdGuard) then sees which sites you look up.
Limits: apps that use their own encrypted DNS (for example some browsers\' secure DNS) or fixed addresses are not filtered, and ads served from the same host as the content cannot be blocked by DNS.

Shizuku lets this app use ADB-level commands without root. Your warranty, banking apps and system updates are not affected.
Install Shizuku from Google Play (developer: RikkaApps) or from its official GitHub page.
Settings → About device → Version → tap Build number seven times and enter your PIN.
Connect to Wi-Fi, then Settings → System → Developer options → Wireless debugging → On.
Open Shizuku → Pairing. In Wireless debugging tap Pair device with pairing code, then type the code into Shizuku\'s notification. Back in Shizuku tap Start.
Come back here and tap Allow. Shizuku asks once.
App info for Shizuku → Battery → Allow background activity. Otherwise OxygenOS may stop it.
Android turns wireless debugging off when the phone restarts, so start Shizuku again (step 4, no new pairing needed). Changes you already made stay in place.

For each app you switch on: exempt it from battery optimization, allow background running, and keep it in the active standby group. This fixes late WhatsApp/Telegram notifications and music or navigation that stops.

Checks every installed app against a public list of known stalkerware, and looks for the capabilities spyware and banking malware need: accessibility control, reading notifications, device admin, hidden icons, SMS access from outside an app store. Nothing leaves your phone.
%1$d apps checked · %2$d need a look · %3$d known stalkerware families in the list
No known stalkerware and no app combines the risky capabilities this scan looks for.
Apps with these powers can see or control what happens on screen. Each one should be an app you chose and trust.
Public list by Echap (stalkerware-indicators, CC BY 4.0). Updating downloads it from GitHub; nothing about your phone is sent.
Could not download the list. Check your connection and try again.
The downloaded list looked wrong and was not used. The current list is kept.
Android\'s built-in malware scanner. Keep it on; this app works alongside it.

Honest limits: Android does not let any app read other apps\' code or files, so no app can promise to find all malware. This scan finds known stalkerware and risky capability combinations; a flagged app is not proof of malware, and a clean result is not a guarantee.
This app\'s package name or signing certificate matches a known stalkerware product. These apps are installed by someone else to secretly read messages, track location and record calls.
Controls the screen through accessibility, can draw over other apps and has SMS access. That combination is what banking trojans use to steal passwords and one-time codes.
Has no icon in the app drawer, yet holds powers such as microphone, background location, accessibility or notification access. Stalkerware typically hides this way.
Can read and control the screen
Accessibility access lets an app see everything on screen and tap for you. Fine for password managers and accessibility tools you chose; dangerous otherwise.
Can read every notification, including messages and login codes.
Device admin can lock or wipe the phone and blocks uninstalling until it is turned off.
SMS access from outside an app store
Was not installed from a known app store and can read or send SMS, which includes bank one-time codes.
Was not installed from a known app store and holds three or more of: microphone, camera, background location, call log, SMS, contacts.
Targets Android 5 or older, so it received its permissions at install time without asking you.
Not from a known app store
Installed from a file, a browser or an unknown source. That is not bad by itself; make sure you installed it on purpose.
Can ask to install further apps. Malware droppers use this to bring in more malware.
A debuggable build. Normal store apps are never debuggable.

Uses Android\'s VPN feature on the phone itself. Choose per app whether to block Wi-Fi, mobile data or both. When you switch networks, only the apps blocked on the new network are routed into the VPN and their traffic is dropped. Every other app connects normally and never passes through it. Nothing is logged or sent anywhere.
Android shows a key icon while it is on. Only one VPN can run at a time, so turning this on stops another VPN app. After a restart, turn it on again, or set it as Always-on VPN.
